pages.page_summary: The page contains a series of physics problems (5.9 through 5.16) covering topics such as power, work, and collisions. It concludes with a diagram (Fig. 5.14) illustrating three possible outcomes of an elastic collision between three identical ball bearings.
knowledge_points: Problem 5.9 asks for the proportionality of power delivered to a body with constant acceleration to time $t$.
Problem 5.10 asks for the proportionality of displacement to time $t$ for a body moving under constant power.
Problem 5.11 involves calculating work done by a constant force $F = -i + 2j + 3k$ N on a body moving 4 m along the z-axis.
Problem 5.12 compares the speeds of an electron (10 keV) and a proton (100 keV) and asks for the ratio of their speeds.
Problem 5.13 calculates work done by gravity and resistive force on a rain drop falling from 500 m.
Problem 5.14 analyzes the momentum conservation and elasticity of a collision between a gas molecule and a wall.
Problem 5.15 calculates the electric power consumed by a pump filling a 30 m³ tank 40 m high in 15 min with 30% efficiency.
Problem 5.16 asks to identify the possible result of an elastic collision between three identical ball bearings as shown in Fig. 5.14.

embedded_text.visual_description: Diagram illustrating three scenarios (i, ii, iii) of a collision between three ball bearings labeled 1, 2, and 3.

visuals.description: A schematic diagram showing the initial state and three possible final states (i, ii, iii) for a collision involving three ball bearings. The initial state shows ball 1 moving with velocity V towards balls 2 and 3 which are in contact. The final states show different velocity distributions and positions.
visuals.educational_role: Illustrates the possible outcomes of an elastic collision between three identical masses to help solve problem 5.16.
